proposals.evidence: Probable regional loan of the Arabic-origin nikāḥ marriage term. Perder Table15 glosses nikā wedding; his examples21,145 and154 concern the marriage ceremony, so the uninformative token gloss nika belongs with that sense, not a personal name. OPED34605 independently attests Pashto nikā, with nikāh/nekāh alternatives, meaning marriage/wedding and labelled Arabic-origin. The h-less donor variant is particularly close, but does not establish Pashto rather than another regional transmission route. Dameli assigns masculine gender in Table15 while Pashto’s dictionary entry is feminine; preserve the Dameli grammar rather than copying donor gender. No direct Arabic edge or specifically Nuristani donor proposed.
